_comment: Cleanup rules. paths: %ENV% vars and {DRIVE} (e.g. C:) are expanded; '*' matches within one folder name. verdict: safe | your-call | keep. action: delete_contents | empty_recycle_bin | null. The app only offers deletion when verdict is 'safe' and an action is set.

rules.title: NVIDIA shader cache (DXCache / GLCache)
rules.explanation: Compiled shaders the driver saves so games load faster. It is rebuilt automatically; the first launch of each game afterwards may stutter briefly.
rules.how_to_free: Delete the folder contents here, or turn on 'Shader Cache Size' limits in the NVIDIA Control Panel.

rules.title: NVIDIA App downloaded updates (ota-artifacts)
rules.explanation: Installer packages the NVIDIA App already downloaded and applied. Old ones are not needed once the update is installed.
rules.how_to_free: Delete the contents. Needs the app to be run as administrator if access is denied.

rules.title: Chrome on-device AI model (OptGuideOnDeviceModel)
rules.explanation: A local AI model (Gemini Nano) Chrome downloads for features like 'Help me write'. Deleting it alone doesn't help: Chrome downloads it again.
rules.how_to_free: In Chrome open chrome://flags, set 'Enables optimization guide on device' to Disabled, restart Chrome, then delete this folder.

rules.title: Application crash dumps
rules.explanation: Memory snapshots saved when programs crashed. Only useful if you are sending them to a developer.

rules.title: Your temporary files (%TEMP%)
rules.explanation: Scratch files programs leave behind. Files currently in use are skipped automatically.
rules.how_to_free: Delete the contents, or use Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.

rules.title: npm package cache
rules.explanation: Copies of every package npm has downloaded. npm re-downloads what it needs on the next install.
rules.how_to_free: Delete the contents, or run: npm cache clean --force

rules.title: VS Code cached extension installers
rules.explanation: Old extension installers and web caches VS Code keeps around. Your installed extensions and settings are not here.
rules.how_to_free: Close VS Code, then delete the contents.

rules.title: Recycle Bin
rules.explanation: Files you already deleted. They still take space until the bin is emptied.
rules.how_to_free: Empty the Recycle Bin (check nothing in it is still needed).

rules.title: Ubisoft Connect patch & cache files
rules.explanation: Downloaded launcher/game patches and cached data that have already been applied. Your installed games and saves live elsewhere.
rules.how_to_free: Quit Ubisoft Connect, then delete the contents. May need administrator rights.

rules.title: Logitech G HUB update cache
rules.explanation: Downloaded firmware and update packages G HUB has already installed. Your device profiles are stored separately.
rules.how_to_free: Quit G HUB from the tray, then delete the contents. May need administrator rights.

rules.title: Hibernation file (hiberfil.sys)
rules.explanation: Holds your memory contents for hibernate and Fast Startup. Windows manages it; never delete it directly.
rules.how_to_free: If you never hibernate: open Terminal as administrator and run  powercfg /h off  (this also disables Fast Startup).

rules.title: Page file (pagefile.sys / swapfile.sys)
rules.explanation: Virtual memory Windows uses when RAM is full. Removing it can cause crashes.
rules.how_to_free: Leave it. If you must, change its size in System Properties > Advanced > Performance > Virtual memory.

rules.title: Windows component store (WinSxS)
rules.explanation: System components and update backups. Many files are hard links shared with C:\Windows, so the real size is smaller than shown. Deleting files here breaks Windows.
rules.how_to_free: Open Terminal as administrator and run  DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup
